name: Bed
overview: Scripture reveals that beds in biblical times varied greatly in material and significance, ranging from simple wooden constructions to elaborate furnishings of gold, silver, ivory, and even iron, as exemplified by Og's iron bedstead (Deuteronomy 3:11) and the luxurious beds described in Esther 1:6. Beds were not only places of rest but also held cultural and symbolic importance, being perfumed for comfort and associated with protection and honor, as seen in Proverbs 7:17 and the guarded bed of Solomon in Song of Solomon 3:7-8. Additionally, beds had a social dimension, as Proverbs 22:27 indicates they were exempt from seizure for debt, underscoring their essential role in personal dignity and security.
